braille.notes: As in Example 16-5, the passage opens with a 5-3-margin transcriber's note explaining that underlining marks footnotes throughout. "staidness" itself is rendered with the underline/emphasis indicator pair (_1...) at its point of reference. The note after the separation line begins with the numeral 1 (^1) and includes the pronunciation respelling in braille phonetic notation ("</@-ad^.bn@+is">); per rule 16.7.3, no second, separately-contracted spelling of "staidness" is added anywhere in the note. A dashed rule ending in reference code #ahh, then a lone '444' continuation marker, close the box (as in Example 16-9).

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.3 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 12645 (the page-change dashed rule ending '#ahh'), stripped of its 9-space left padding, is exactly 40 characters. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
